title: Tuchel's World Cup Bombshell: Foden, Palmer, Alexander-Arnold Axed
summary: When England manager Thomas Tuchel revealed his 26-man squad for this summer's World Cup, the list was missing some household names. Phil Foden, Cole Palmer, and Trent Alexander-Arnold—three of the Premier League's most recognizable talents—were all left out. The decision sent shockwaves through the soccer world. Harry Maguire, the Manchester United defender, expressed his dismay on Instagram: 'I was confident I could have played a major part this summer for my country after the season I've had. I've been left shocked and gutted by the decision.' His mother, Zoe, went further, calling the omission 'disgusted' in a social media post. Luke Shaw, another United player, was also omitted despite an impressive season. Tuchel's selections reflect a mix of form and tactical preference. Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins earned his spot after a Europa League-winning campaign. Ivan Toney, now playing in Saudi Arabia, was rewarded for a staggering 32 goals in 32 league games. Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White, the top-scoring Englishman in the Premier League with 14 goals, missed out—a decision that raised eyebrows. Defensively, Tuchel opted for Newcastle's Dan Burn and Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly over more experienced options. Tottenham's Djed Spence, who recently suffered a broken jaw, was included and may play with a protective mask. Meanwhile, Real Madrid's Alexander-Arnold and Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly were overlooked. John Stones, despite an injury-hit season, kept his place as Tuchel views him as crucial. Kobbie Mainoo also retained his spot after a recall. The squad now carries the weight of a nation's expectations, with fans debating whether Tuchel's bold calls will pay off on the biggest stage.
why_it_matters: This story shows how even top athletes face rejection, and how coaches must make difficult choices that can spark intense debate. For a young person, it highlights that talent alone isn't always enough—attitude, form, and fitting a system matter too—and that responding to disappointment with grace, or not, can shape public perception.

keywords.explanation: Dismay is a feeling of shock and unhappiness when something bad happens.
An omission is something that has been left out or not included.
Tactical means related to a carefully planned method to achieve a goal, especially in sports or military operations.
Staggering means very surprising and almost hard to believe because it is so large or extreme.
If something raises eyebrows, it causes surprise or disapproval.
In sports, a recall is when a player is chosen again to play for a team after being left out.

background_read: England's men's national football team has not won the FIFA World Cup (the biggest international football tournament, held every four years) since 1966, and the country places enormous expectations on its manager to end that drought.
Thomas Tuchel (a German coach who won the UEFA Champions League with Chelsea in 2021) was appointed England manager in 2025 with a clear mission: to build a squad capable of winning the World Cup.

His decision to drop stars like Phil Foden (the 2024 Premier League Player of the Season) and Trent Alexander-Arnold (who recently moved to Real Madrid, one of the world's top clubs) shocked many, but reflects a common tension in sports—choosing players based on current form and tactical fit rather than reputation.

The public reaction, including Harry Maguire’s mother calling the omission 'disgusted' on social media, shows how personal these choices become for players and their families, and how social media amplifies that emotion.

perspectives.description: Tuchel based his picks on current form and tactical fit, not reputation. This could lead to a more cohesive, hungry team capable of surprising the world and finally lifting the World Cup.
Dropping fan favorites risks alienating the squad and upsetting team chemistry. The public anger from a veteran like Maguire and his family shows the emotional cost, which could hurt morale.

This is a classic manager’s dilemma: balancing star power with system needs. Soccer history is full of controversial squad picks that either backfired or became genius moves—only time reveals which label applies.

The pressure on Tuchel is now immense. If England underperforms, the criticism will be fierce and his job could be at risk; if they succeed, these bold omissions will be remembered as masterstrokes that reshaped the team.
